predecessors.name: Soomra dynasty
predecessors.text: Sindh, the Soomra realm: 'The Sammas overthrew the Soomras soon after 1335'

predecessors.name: Tughlaq dynasty
predecessors.text: Sindh, from which Muhammad bin Tughluq's army withdrew after he 'died at Sondha' in 1351

successors.name: Arghun dynasty
successors.text: Sindh, taken by Shah Beg Arghun in the 1520 campaign that 'marked the end of Samma rule in Sindh'

ledger.x: 1351: the Sammas rule an independent Sindh.
1520: Jam Feroz is beaten and flees to Gujarat; Thatta is sacked 'during the 1520 campaign'.

wars.name: Muhammad bin Tughluq's Sindh expedition
wars.outcome: Muhammad died at Sondha in March 1351 pursuing rebels and tax resisters; the Sammas became independent.

wars.name: Firuz Shah's Thatta campaigns
wars.outcome: Firuz marched in 1362, retreated, and had Thatta's submission and a tribute of 400,000 tankas in 1363 (his page); the Samma page has attacks in 1365 and 1367 'without success' and then Banbhiniyo's surrender, the Sammas 'again subject to Delhi for a time'.

wars.name: Arghun raid on Sindh
wars.outcome: 'After 1490, a Mughal army under Shah Beg Arghun raided into Samma territory'; Darya Khan defeated it at Duruh-i-Kureeb and the raiders did not return in Nizamuddin's reign.

wars.name: Arghun conquest of Sindh
wars.outcome: Shah Beg Arghun defeated Jam Feroz, who fled to Gujarat, and sacked Thatta; Samma rule ended.

certainty.note: The Indus delta and the Thar frontier are approximate; no page gives a boundary, and Multan (Langahs), Kutch and Bhakkar are the edges the page names.
